speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your current symptoms of right knee pain and swelling, and tell me more about the specific pain you experience when urinating.

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (Reiter's Syndrome). The clinical triad of asymmetric oligoarthritis (knee, ankle), urethritis, and risk factors (sexual activity, inconsistent condom use) strongly supports this diagnosis; I will request HLA-B27, urine culture, and knee synovial fluid analysis to confirm.
